events.region: Glacier Bay; Eastern Chichagof Island; Cape Fairweather to Lisianski Strait; City and Borough of Sitka; Admiralty Island; City and Borough of Juneau; Petersburg Borough; Western Kupreanof and Kuiu Island; Prince of Wales Island; City and Borough of Wrangell; Ketchikan Gateway Borough; Annette Island
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
A stronger weather system is expected to move into the panhandle
Saturday into Sunday, bringing periods of moderate to heavy rain.
The peak of heavier rainfall is forecast overnight Saturday, when
rain rates could exceed 0.15 inches per hour. The most significant
rainfall is anticipated to continue at any given location for a
period of 12-18 hours before decreasing.

Total rainfall accumulations for the event are expected to be
between 1.5 and 3.0 inches, with the greatest amounts in the central
panhandle. Upwards of 5 inches is possible for higher elevations.
Due to the short nature of the heavier rainfall, smaller creeks and
streams will rise quickly, but are not expected to flood.

events.region: North Walton; Central Walton; Holmes; Washington; Inland Bay; Inland Gulf; South Walton; Coastal Bay; Coastal Gulf
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Portions of the Florida Panhandle, including the following
areas, Central Walton, Coastal Gulf, Holmes, Coastal Bay, Inland
Bay, Inland Gulf, North Walton, South Walton and Washington.

* WHEN...From 11 AM EDT  /10 AM CDT/ this morning through Monday
morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Multiple rounds of heavy rainfall are expected Saturday afternoon
through at least early Monday morning. Additional rainfall
amounts of 3 to 6 inches of rain are expected with locally higher
amounts of up to 10 inches possible. This may lead to flash
flooding, especially in urban and poor drainage areas.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
